reviewed_by: Claude review of selected-skill instructions in the Jev request
reason: Jev ranked the deferred catalog from the operator's messages alone: a turn driven by a selected skill sent the skill's name only if the operator happened to type it, while the skill body - the steps that say which tools the turn needs - stayed in the system instructions. build_state now carries the newest selected skills as operator_selected_skills, redacted with the same redact_text pass as messages and bounded to 4 skills, 6k chars each and 12k chars total so state plus the longest choice question stays inside Jev's 32k window; the gate and choice questions gain a clause naming that key only when it is present, so skill-free turns keep byte-identical wording and the tuned thresholds. The receipt records which skills were sent, including on a failed call, so the turn snapshot documents the egress. The selection runs test_tool_suggestions for the new state, questions, receipt and the prepare-level wiring, and test_chat because chat.py now passes its snapshots into that call.
exclusions: No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No screenshot baselines: the only rendered change is one sentence of consent copy inside the existing #tool-suggestions-option label, which the area's journeys screenshot as an output artifact, not a compared baseline. ui/src/api/types.ts is unmapped by ui/playwright-impact.json but the change there is a doc comment, so it selects nothing on its own. area:assistant (matched through src/nebula/v3/chat.py) is excluded: chat.py's only change is the skills= argument on the Jev call, with no transcript, routing or rendering behaviour touched, and tests/v3/test_chat.py plus area:tool-suggestions cover that path. tests/test_playwright_impact.py is excluded because ui/playwright-impact.json is unchanged. No full suites.
